question: Spain has issued a Royal Decree requiring a V16 warning light connected to a state platform (DGT 3.0) to be installed in all vehicles as the only piece of hazard warning equipment from January 2026. That obligation entails specific technical requirements, connectivity and standardisation linked to national infrastructure.

Given that the European Union has not harmonised ways to signal a hazard or required that triangles or other devices be used, and that Regulation (EU) 2019/515 requires that products lawfully marketed in other Member States be mutually recognised: 1.
Has Spain issued the correct notification of those technical requirements under Directive 2015/1535, and what would be the consequences of a failure to do so?
Does the Commission consider that imposing a single national model could constitute a measure with equivalent effect to restricting the marketing of alternative devices, contrary to Article 34 TFEU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.2.2026) The mandatory use of V-16 hazard signalling devices in vehicles in circulation on public roads in Spain from 1 January 2026 as well as the requirement that each device communicates its geolocation to the Directorate-General for Transport (DGT), have been laid down in Spanish Royal Decree 159/20211 and Royal Decree 1030/20222.

Neither of these Decrees have been notified under the Directive (EU) 2015/15353 procedure. It is for the Member States to assess if their draft measures are subject to the notification requirement under Directive (EU) 2015/1535.

Where Member States fail to meet their obligation to communicate draft technical regulations under Article 5(1) of Directive (EU) 2015/1535, the Commission can launch enforcement actions under Article 258 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU).

Additionally, as held by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU), national courts must decline to apply technical regulations that have not been notified to the Commission in accordance with Directive (EU) 2015/15354. The use of hazard signalling devices is not harmonised at EU level and the national traffic rules of the Member States apply instead.

Nevertheless, imposing specific technical requirements on the device at national level may constitute a measure with equivalent effect to trade restriction in the Internal Market under Article 34 TFEU, which the Spanish authorities would have to justify under Article 36 of TFEU or on the basis of one of the mandatory requirements developed in the CJEU’s jurisprudence.
